title: GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization
text: We compare GDPO and GRPO by training DeepSeek-R1-7B on the Eurus-2-RL dataset [ 28 ] , which contains 24k coding problems, each with multiple test cases. Training is conducted using the verl [ 19 ] framework for 400 steps, and we adopt the same hyperparameter configuration used in the mathematical reasoning experiments. The training optimizes three rewards: Passrate reward: The passrate reward ℛ pass ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \mathcal{R}_{\text{pass}}\in[0,1] measures the proportion of test cases passed by the generated code: Conditioned Length reward: The length reward ℛ ~ length ∈ { 0 , 1 } \mathcal{\tilde{R}}_{\text{length}}\in\{0,1\} checks whether the model’s response remains within the target length l l and whether the generated code satisfies correctness requirements: Bug reward: The bug reward ℛ bug ∈ { 0 , 1 } \mathcal{R}_{\text{bug}}\in\{0,1\} indicates whether the generated code runs without runtime or compilation errors. For evaluation, we assess the trained model on the validation set from PRIME [ 28 ] , which includes Apps [ 29 ] , CodeContests [ 30 ] , Codeforces 2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/datasets/MatrixStudio/Codeforces-Python-Submissions , and Taco [ 31 ] .
